item.title: Light meson decays at BESIII
item.description: arXiv:2610.24472v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The world's largest sample of $J/\psi$ events accumulated with the BESIII detector offers a unique opportunity to investigate $\eta$ and $\eta'$ physics via the radiative transition processes $J/\psi \to \gamma\eta/\eta'$. A selection of recent highlights in light meson spectroscopy achieved at BESIII is reviewed in these proceedings, including evidence for the cusp effect in $\eta' \to \pi^0\pi^0\eta$, precision studies of the decay mechanisms of $\eta \to 3\pi$ and $\eta' \to 4\pi$, electromagnetic transition form factor measurements with $\eta/\eta' \to \gamma e^+e^-$ and $\eta' \to \pi^+\pi^-l^+l^-$, as well as searches for rare decays of $\eta$ and $\eta'$ into lepton pairs, including $\eta \to l^+l^-$ and $\eta/\eta' \to l^+l^-l^+l^-$~($l = e, \mu$).
item.dc:creator: Kailu Li

item.title: ceci n'est pas un tagger, can an LLM flavour-tag a jet?
item.description: arXiv:2610.24954v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly capable of reasoning about scientific problems, effectively mastering and synthesizing entire fields of research and providing, for the first time, access to a distilled and queryable form of scientific knowledge. As the integration of LLMs rapidly spreads across the large collaborations of high-energy physics, aiming to re-think and optimize analysis workflows, it remains unclear whether the knowledge acquired during pretraining can support quantitative inference on physical data. Moving beyond the applications currently pursued by the community, we pose a simple question: can an LLM classify the flavour of a hadronic jet? An LLM is therefore asked to assign flavour probabilities (b, c, light, $\tau$) to jets from a public ATLAS flavour-tagging sample, using only reconstructed constituents. Under a small set of constraints, the model is not allowed to write code or implement conventional algorithms and must instead perform the inference directly from its pretrained knowledge and the available inputs. We report two complementary results and make publicly available, through a GitHub repository, all the code required to reproduce the experiment and obtain the quantitative results presented in this work. First, the model achieves non-trivial discrimination between flavours, which we compare with recent ATLAS flavour-tagging algorithms. Second, the model accompanies each prediction with a natural language rationale. The physical concepts invoked in these rationales correlate with the truth flavour and reproduce the features traditionally associated with each jet category. Flavour tagging thus provides a laboratory for broader questions: how can we actively leverage the corpus of scientific knowledge accumulated over decades of research? Could LLMs serve as a general source of scientific context for task-specific algorithms?
item.dc:creator: Andrea Coccaro, Andrea Milici, Lucio Derin

item.title: Search for new physics with charm data at BESIII
item.description: arXiv:2610.25753v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Up to now, the Standard Model (SM) remains confronted with several outstanding issues, including the matter-antimatter asymmetry in the universe, as well as the masses, oscillations, and hierarchical structure of neutrinos. These challenges are closely tied to the naturalness and stability of the SM, and have motivated numerous proposals for new physics beyond the SM. The BESIII experiment has accumulated the world's largest data samples at the $J/\psi$ and $\psi(3686)$ resonances, providing an ideal environment for probing signatures of physics beyond the SM. This proceeding presents a summary of recent results published by the BESIII Collaboration on the searches for lepton/baryon number violation (LNV/BNV), charged lepton flavor violation (CLFV), and charmonium weak decays.
item.dc:creator: Xinyu Chai (on behalf of the BESIII Collaboration)

item.title: Low-Latency Beam-Background Suppression for the BESIII Trigger System Using Machine Learning Trained on Experimental Data
item.description: arXiv:2610.26148v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Beam-induced backgrounds contribute to the trigger and data-acquisition rate at high-luminosity electron-positron colliders. Their dependence on beam and machine conditions motivates data-driven studies alongside simulation. A data-driven machine-learning method for trigger-level beam-background suppression is developed using experimental data recorded by BESIII. Compact neural-network classifiers are trained and evaluated for two trigger configurations: one based only on tracking and time-of-flight information, and one based only on electromagnetic-calorimeter information. Each classifier uses 48 binary Level-1 trigger conditions of the BESIII detector. The models distinguish hadron events from beam-background events and are evaluated against the established trigger selection at matched hadron-event efficiency. Relative to the established trigger selection, the beam-background false-positive rate is reduced by 20-60% across the studied configurations and center-of-mass energies, with stable suppression performance as tested using random-trigger data. Hardware-oriented synthesis indicates that the compact network is suitable for low-latency FPGA implementation. The proposed method can reduce the fraction of beam-background events in the trigger stream in future BESIII trigger upgrades. It also provides a reference for trigger optimization at future high-luminosity electron-positron colliders.
item.dc:creator: Hanlin Zhang, Minggang Zhao, Junhao Yin, Boping Chen, Jingzhou Zhao, Wenxuan Gong, Ke Li

item.title: Measurements of time-dependent b-hadron properties in LHCb
item.description: arXiv:2610.26188v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: These proceedings present the latest measurements of time-dependent properties of $b$-hadrons using the LHCb Run 2 data set. Three results are presented. The first of these is a measurement of the CKM phase $\phi_s$ with $B_s^0\to J/\psi\pi^+\pi^-$. This result improves the determination in this channel, obtaining a result of $\phi_s = -77\pm34(\text{stat})\pm7(\text{syst})$ mrad. This result is included in the LHCb global average to obtain $\phi_s = -41\pm17$ mrad. Additionally, a determination of the penguin contributions, $\Delta\phi_s$, to measurements of $\phi_s$ using $B^0\to J/\psi\rho^0(770)$ is presented. This measurement constitutes the first observation of CP-violation in $B_0 \to J/\psi\rho^0(770)$ decays. The CKM phase $2\beta$ is measured and is determined to be $2\beta^{\text{eff}}_{ccd} = 0.710\pm0.084\pm0.051$ rad. The most stringent constraint on penguin contributions is obtained and determined to be $\Delta\phi_s = 5.0\pm4.6$ mrad. Finally, the first measurement of time-dependent CP-violation in a $b\to s l^+ l^-$ process using the decay $B_s^0 \to K_S \mu^+ \mu^- $ is presented. The time-dependent coefficients of this decay are determined to be $C=-0.13\pm0.32(\text{stat})\pm0.04(\text{syst})$ and $S=+0.82\pm0.29(\text{stat})\pm0.05(\text{syst})$.
item.dc:creator: Lucas Foreman

item.title: Neural Bayesian Online Calibration with Deficient Simulators for MADMAX Dark Matter Experiment
item.description: arXiv:2610.26343v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Scientific experiments often rely on deficient simulators and hardware whose commanded settings differ from the states realized in practice, limiting reliable optimization and inference. A Bayesian online calibration framework is introduced for experiments with at least one directly measurable simulator output and potentially latent quantities of scientific interest. Pre-calibration data are used to learn state-dependent effective simulator parameters, while a normalizing flow enables amortized posterior inference from measurement histories. During calibration, measurement and positioning uncertainties are propagated, and hardware commands are selected by balancing expected improvement with information gain. The framework is applied to the MADMAX dark matter experiment, where measured reflectivity is used to calibrate a deficient disk-booster simulator and infer the unobservable axion-signal power boost factor. Experimental validation on the MADMAX experiment is ongoing.
item.dc:creator: Nabil Salama

item.title: Measurement of the relative phase between the strong and electromagnetic amplitudes in $\boldsymbol{J/\psi \to \Sigma^{+} \bar{\Sigma}^{-}}$
item.description: arXiv:2610.26673v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Using 284 pb$^{-1}$ of $e^{+}e^{-}$ collision data collected with the BESIII detector at center-of-mass energies between 3.00 and 3.12 GeV, the relative phase between the strong and electromagnetic interaction amplitudes in the process $J/\psi \to \Sigma^+ \bar{\Sigma}^-$ is determined. The relative phase is measured to be $(107.9 \pm 24.9)^{\circ}$ or $(-107.6 \pm 24.3)^{\circ}$, where the uncertainty includes both statistical and systematic sources. This is the first experimental determination of the strong-electromagnetic phase difference in $J/\psi$ decays to a hyperon-antihyperon pair. The branching fraction $\mathcal{B}_{J/\psi \to \Sigma^+ \bar{\Sigma}^-}$ is measured to be $(1.14 \pm 0.04)\times 10^{-3}$ for the positive phase solution or $(1.19 \pm 0.04) \times 10^{-3}$ for the negative phase solution. These results provide important input for testing perturbative QCD predictions and studies of SU(3) flavor symmetry.

item.title: BeAGLE++: A modern modular framework for eA physics at the EIC
item.description: arXiv:2610.24095v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present the Benchmark eA Generator for LEptoproduction (BeAGLE++), a next-generation, general-purpose Monte Carlo event generator for high-energy lepton-nucleus collisions and the successor to BeAGLE. The framework incorporates a formation-zone intranuclear cascade to describe hadronic final-state interactions (FSIs), followed by statistical de-excitation of the residual nucleus. Compared with the legacy implementation, the BeAGLE++ cascade introduces a discrete time-ordered treatment of hadronic interactions and light-cluster production during intranuclear transport. Comparisons with E665 measurements and legacy BeAGLE calculations show broad agreement for selected observables, while revealing differences in final states sensitive to FSIs. These differences provide opportunities to assess the model dependence of nuclear-breakup predictions and constrain the underlying cascade dynamics. With its modular architecture, BeAGLE++ provides a flexible simulation framework for the Electron-Ion Collider (EIC) and a platform for developing and testing new physics models against existing data and future EIC measurements.
item.dc:creator: Arjun Kumar, Abhay Deshpande, Zhoudunming Tu

item.title: Development of microwave multiplexed readout for athermal phonon TES-based detectors
item.description: arXiv:2610.24300v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Continued advancements in sub-eV calorimetric measurements are being enabled through the athermal phonon detection channel, with applications spanning a diverse array of fields, including low-mass dark matter searches, coherent elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering, and quantum information science. While Transition Edge Sensors (TESs) have achieved the lowest thresholds to date, they face significant scalability bottlenecks due to the inherent constraints of conventional SQUID readout architectures. To address this limitation, we present an update on R&D to develop practical, highly multiplexed, microwave readout for athermal phonon TESs, which can enable a dramatic increase in both sensor count and target mass, with a focus on sub-GeV dark matter searches as a target application. This work leverages advances from highly scaled mm-wave, x-ray, and gamma-ray TES systems, adapting them to the unique needs of low-threshold rare event measurements. We quantify the basic readout functionality and noise level in our dilution refrigerator testbed and demonstrate operation of a variety of TES devices with saturation powers significantly lower than mm-wave and x-ray devices. We demonstrate proof-of-concept multiplexed readout of background event pulses, bound the readout's contribution to the parasitic TES background load to <1 fW, and discuss a cryogenic inline RF filtering scheme. These results demonstrate practical solutions to several of the key challenges that must be solved before a next-generation athermal phonon detector at scale is realized.

item.title: Collider event distances from the phase space sphere
item.description: arXiv:2610.24319v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Can the distribution of collider events in phase space be used to distinguish the processes that produced them? We present a distance-based classification method that uses the global topology of Lorentz-invariant phase space and retains reconstructed masses. To tackle particularly challenging classification tasks that may benefit from higher event resolution, we develop a polynomial-time approximation to compute the distances. The resulting classifiers achieve strong discrimination across several simulated benchmarks, including fully hadronic four-top production against $t\bar t+\text{jets}$.
item.dc:creator: Nathaniel Craig, Brian Henning, Andrew J. Larkoski, I\~nigo Valenzuela Lombera

item.title: Common origin of the Belle-BESIII line-shape difference of $\Lambda_c^+\bar{\Lambda}_c^-$, $D_s D_{s1}$ and $D_s D_{s2}^*$ from $e^+ e^-$ annihilation
item.description: arXiv:2610.24634v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The longstanding Belle--BESIII discrepancies in the $e^+e^-\to\Lambda_c^+\bar\Lambda_c^-$, $D_sD_{s1}(2536)$, and $D_sD_{s2}^{*}(2573)$ line shapes remain an unresolved puzzle, with enhancements observed by Belle that are absent or much weaker in the BESIII measurements. In this work, we propose a new mechanism based on the radiative production of higher charmonia to explain these differences. Such processes may contribute to Belle's initial-state radiation samples, and the luminosity normalization increases their contribution to the extracted cross sections. With the vector contributions scaled by BESIII data, a pseudoscalar charmonium $\eta_c(6S)$ contribution can describe the baryonic enhancement, while an introduced $\chi_{c2}(5P)$ contribution can describe the enhancements in both meson channels. This mechanism offers a possible common explanation for these differences and, as a bonus, suggests a way to search for missing higher charmonia at Belle II.
item.dc:creator: Cheng-Xi Liu, Tian-Le Gao, Cheng-Ping Shen, Xiang Liu

item.title: Global analyses of PDFs in the precision era
item.description: arXiv:2610.24691v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Parton distribution functions or PDFs are determined through global fits to an ever-increasing array of data, including deep-inelastic scattering at fixed-target experiments and HERA, and hadron collisions at the Tevatron and LHC. As the dataset has expanded, theoretical accuracy has improved from partial next-to-next-to-leading order (NNLO) coverage about 20 years ago to approximate N$^3$LO global fits today. The fitting collaborations must reconcile these complex calculations and data analyses while ensuring that quoted PDF uncertainty bands remain reliable.
item.dc:creator: Juan M. Cruz-Martinez

item.title: Where should we look for the deviation from quantum mechanics?
item.description: arXiv:2610.24857v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We argue that the experimental measurement of the lifetime and decay law of metastable helium is a promising way to find a deviation from quantum mechanics. We analyze the decay of the metastable state for a quartic deformation of quantum mechanics. We find that the absolute change of the mean lifetime can be significant even if the modification is small. We show that, in the Wigner--Weisskopf approximation, the deviation from the exponential law in the modified theory can occur on time scales comparable with the lifetime.
item.dc:creator: Jerome Nicolas, Albert Schwarz

item.title: Where are the higher excited $B$ and $B_s$ mesons with coupled-channel effects?
item.description: arXiv:2610.25125v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Inspired by the newly observed $B_{s0}^*(5700)^0$, whose mass agrees well with our previous unquenched prediction for $B_s(1^3P_0)$ [Phys.~Rev.~D \textbf{109}, 116006 (2024)], we study the mass spectra and OZI-allowed two-body strong decays of the higher $3S$-, $2P$-, $2D$-, and $1F$-wave $B$ and $B_s$ mesons in the same unquenched quark model. Our results show that coupled-channel effects significantly lower the masses and modify the relative level spacings. The scalar state $B(2^3P_0)$ is strongly affected: its mass is lowered well below the quenched quark model predictions, and it mainly decays into $B\pi$. Furthermore, the mass ordering of the vector states $B(2^3D_1)$ and $B(3^3S_1)$ is reversed, and the lighter $B(2^3D_1)$ state mainly decays into $B_1(5721)\pi$. To test these results, the $B(2^3P_0)$ and $B(2^3D_1)$ states are worth searching for in the $B\pi$ and $B_1(5721)\pi$ channels, respectively. In addition, some higher excitations are predicted to be relatively narrow and can be searched for in the $B^{(*)}\pi$, $B^{(*)}K$, $B_1(5721)\pi/K$, and $B_2^*(5747)\pi/K$ channels. These predictions provide useful references for future experimental searches and help clarify the role of coupled-channel effects in the heavy-light meson spectrum.
item.dc:creator: Ru-Hui Ni, Jia-Jun Wu, Xian-Hui Zhong

item.title: Is there gluonium in the $\eta^\prime$? The flavour structure of $\eta$ and $\eta^\prime$ mixing in radiative $V\to P\gamma$ and $P\to V\gamma$ decays
item.description: arXiv:2610.25216v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Radiative $V\to P\gamma$ and $P\to V\gamma$ decays are conventionally described using constituent-quark mass differences and phenomenological wavefunction-overlap factors as sources of flavour-symmetry breaking. We investigate whether the overlap factors can instead be understood as the effect of mixing of the $\eta$ and $\eta^\prime$ with an additional pseudoscalar state, described by an $SO(4)$ rotation among four basis states. A global fit to current data yields a significantly better description than the corresponding three-state limit without overlap factors, while preserving the established $\eta$-$\eta^\prime$ and vector-meson mixing angles, and shows that the additional state mixes predominantly with the non-strange component. The conventional overlap-factor description is recovered exactly as the special case in which this mixing is purely non-strange. The non-strange pattern disfavours both a flavour-singlet admixture, as expected from mixing with a pseudoscalar glueball, and the gluonium scenario considered in previous analyses. Radiative decays therefore provide no compelling evidence for gluonium in the $\eta^\prime$, and the overlap factors are better interpreted in terms of a radially excited non-strange state.
item.dc:creator: Rafel Escribano, Emilio Royo

item.title: Probing the two-pole structure of the $D_0^*(2300)$ with an $SU(3)$ flavor filter
item.description: arXiv:2610.26175v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We propose an $SU(3)$ flavor-filtering strategy to resolve the two-pole structure associated with the $D_0^*(2300)$ and to probe its flavor-sextet component directly in invariant-mass distributions. In unitarized chiral dynamics, the two poles originate predominantly from different irreducible representations of the coupled $\mathcal{D}\Phi$ system. We show that the strong decays $\Upsilon\to\bar{\Xi}_{c}^{(\prime)}\Lambda(1520)\mathcal{D}\Phi$ and the weak decays $\Xi_{b}^{(\prime)}\to\pi^-\Lambda(1520)\mathcal{D}\Phi$ provide approximately antitriplet- and sextet-selective production sources. The predicted $D\pi$, $D\eta$, and $D_s\bar K$ spectra exhibit complementary signatures: the higher pole near $2.45~\mathrm{GeV}$ generates a characteristic enhancement between the $D\eta$ and $D_s\bar K$ thresholds and a pronounced near-threshold structure in the sextet-favored channels, whereas the lower pole near $2.1~\mathrm{GeV}$ dominates the antitriplet-favored channels. The contrast between these line shapes directly reflects the flavor representation selected by the corresponding cascade-baryon tag. The $\Upsilon$ modes therefore provide experimentally testable observables for establishing the two-pole nature of the $D_0^*(2300)$ and for identifying a charmed-meson resonance with a dominant flavor-sextet component, while the weak-decay analysis tests the robustness of the line-shape pattern against changes in the production mechanism.
item.dc:creator: Ying-Bo He, Liu-Lin Wang, Xiao-Hai Liu, Qiang Zhao

item.title: Characterization of the R14374-10 photomultiplier tube for the Pacific Ocean Neutrino Experiment
item.description: arXiv:2610.26299v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Pacific Ocean Neutrino Experiment (P-ONE) is a planned cubic-kilometer-scale neutrino telescope that will be deployed in the Pacific Ocean, leveraging deep-sea infrastructure operated by Ocean Networks Canada (ONC). The first detector line will deploy 320 3-inch Hamamatsu R14374-10 photomultiplier tubes (PMTs) to detect Cherenkov light produced by charged particles propagating through water, as well as light from calibration sources and optical backgrounds. This article presents the systematic characterization of all PMTs to be integrated into the first detector line prior to deployment, ensuring compliance with all detector acceptance criteria. All PMTs satisfy the specified performance criteria: the average transit-time spread (TTS) was measured to be $1.73\pm 0.15\,$ns, and the average charge resolution at a gain of \num{5e6} was $0.43\pm 0.03\,$pC; the average after-pulse rate was measured to be around 6$\,\%$. The integrated P-ONE data acquisition (DAQ) system was also tested and cross-validated against a laboratory digitization system. The second part of the paper presents an in-depth characterization of a subset of six PMTs, focusing on the key properties required for detector simulations, including linearity, after-pulse rate, quantum efficiency, and relative collection efficiency. PMT linearity was measured at a gain of \num{5e6} using the complete P-ONE readout electronics, and the response was found to remain linear for signals up to 150 photoelectrons. After-pulse contributions from $\text{Cs}^{+}$, $\text{He}^{+}$, and other ions were identified in the subset. The peak quantum efficiency was measured to be $27.0\pm0.7\,\%$ at 395\,nm. Using measurements of the relative detection efficiency, the collection efficiency was found to differ by a wavelength-independent offset of 10--15$\%$ across the measured wavelength range.

item.title: The NLL/NLO$^+$ QCD spectrum from Higgs-plus-charm correlations at the LHC
item.description: arXiv:2610.26373v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate the high-energy behavior of observables sensitive to the production of a Higgs boson in association with a singly charmed hadron at the $\sqrt{s}=14$ TeV LHC, with light-flavored hadrons considered for comparison. Our reference formalism is the hybrid factorization at NLL/NLO$^+$, where the standard collinear picture is enhanced by the resummation of energy logarithms at the next-to-leading level and beyond. We present a prime phenomenological application of the next-to-leading correction to the singly off-shell Higgs emission function, as implemented in the multimodular JETHAD interface, a core element to test the stability of our high-energy distributions under energy-scale variations and to assess the weight of missing higher-order uncertainties. The resulting natural stability traces our path towards precision studies of Higgs production within high-energy next-to-leading-order QCD.
item.dc:creator: Francesco Giovanni Celiberto, Francesca Lonigro

item.title: HERA at low-x
item.description: arXiv:2610.26393v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The field of Deep Inelastic Scattering is introduced with particular reference to the High Energy Ring Accelerator HERA. The formalism of the Quark Parton Model and its extension in perturbative Quantum Chromodynamics is outlined, defining the concept of a Parton Distribution Function. The HERA data on inclusive and semi-inclusive processes are reviewed with particular emphasis on results at low x and low Q 2 . Their theoretical imterpretation in terms of conventional QCD DGLAP evolution and its extension to BFKL evolution in the low-x regime is explored together with the possibility of the onset of a new non-linear regime which may lead to gluon saturation. The focus then moves to diffractive processes both quasi-elastic and diffractive dissociation, where more detailed hints of saturation are found.
item.dc:creator: A M Cooper-Sarkar, P R Newman

item.title: Optical imaging in dual-phase xenon time projection chambers for neutrinoless double beta decay searches
item.description:
arXiv:2610.26739v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Dual-phase xenon time projection chambers (TPCs) are the leading technology for WIMP dark matter searches and have also demonstrated competitive sensitivities to neutrinoless double beta decays (0$
u eta eta$) of \ce{^{136}Xe}. However, the large energy disparity between these two signals requires different detector optimizations. In particular, 0$
u eta eta$\ searches in liquid xenon desire efficient rejection of closely located multiscatters of background gamma rays near the 0$
u eta eta$\ energy, a capability achieved only in the vertical dimension in existing dual-phase xenon TPCs. We propose a highly customized, wide-angle optical system that can be conveniently integrated into large xenon TPCs and provide mm-scale transverse position resolution for MeV signals by imaging gas electroluminescence light. This approach preserves a TPC's low-energy sensitivity and optimizes a single experiment for both dark matter and 0$
u eta eta$\ searches. This paper discusses the design, simulated performance, and implications of the imaging system for future liquid xenon-based 0$
u eta eta$\ searches.
item.dc:creator: Adam D. Tidball, Jingke Xu, Brian G. Lenardo, Nicholas Antipa

item.title: First observation of weak magnetism in neutron decay
item.description: arXiv:2610.26792v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Weak magnetism, introduced by Gell-Mann as a hallmark consequence of the conserved vector current (CVC) hypothesis, has remained unobserved in the decay of the free neutron, the simplest $\beta$-decay system. The reason is that the relevant observable, the $\beta$ asymmetry, cannot separate the weak-magnetism form factor $g_M$ from the axial-to-vector ratio $\lambda$. We show that this degeneracy is lifted by combining the $\beta$ asymmetry measurements with the neutron lifetime and the $\mathcal{F}t$ value of superallowed $0^+\to0^+$ decays. Current data yield $g_M = 4.47(87)$, in agreement with the CVC prediction of $4.71$ and excluding the absence of weak magnetism at the $5.1\sigma$ level. Importantly, the significance remains between $5.0\sigma$ and $6.1\sigma$ for all considered variations of the neutron dataset, despite its well-known internal tensions. We further show that, under present experimental conditions, a full analysis of the energy dependence of the asymmetry would improve the $g_M$ extraction by only a few percent. These results constitute the first observation of weak magnetism in the decay of the free neutron nearly seven decades after Gell-Mann's prediction.
item.dc:creator: Miriam Camarasa-Domene, Mart\'in Gonz\'alez-Alonso, Mart\'in Novoa-Brunet

item.title: Measurements and models of enhanced recombination following inner-shell vacancies in liquid xenon
item.description: arXiv:2503.05679v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Electron-capture decays of $^{125}$Xe and $^{127}$Xe, and double-electron-capture decays of $^{124}$Xe, are backgrounds in searches for weakly interacting massive particles (WIMPs) conducted by dual-phase xenon time projection chambers such as LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ). These decays produce signals with more light and less charge than equivalent-energy $\beta$ decays, and correspondingly overlap more with WIMP signals. We measure three electron-capture charge yields in LZ: the 1.1~keV M-shell, 5.2~keV L-shell, and 33.2~keV K-shell at drift fields of 193 and 96.5~V/cm. The LL double-electron-capture decay of $^{124}$Xe exhibits even more pronounced shifts in charge and light. We provide a first model of double-electron-capture charge yields using the link between ionization density and electron-ion recombination, and identify a need for more accurate calculations. Finally, we discuss the implications of the reduced charge yield of these decays and other interactions creating inner-shell vacancies for future dark matter searches.

item.title: Agentic AI -- Physicist Collaboration in Experimental Particle Physics: A Proof-of-Concept Measurement with LEP Open Data
item.description: arXiv:2603.05735v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present an agentic measurement of the thrust distribution in $e^{+}e^{-}$ collisions at $\sqrt{s}=91.2$ GeV using ALEPH archived data. This work was carried out through an AI agent-physicist collaboration, using interactive natural-language prompting of Anthropic Claude and OpenAI Codex. Under physicist guidance, the agents wrote and executed all analysis code and drafted the majority of the text included in this paper. A fully-corrected thrust spectrum is obtained via Iterative Bayesian Unfolding and Monte Carlo based corrections. The principal contribution of this work is the demonstration of the agentic analysis, with thrust serving as a benchmark observable for the method. Dedicated precision measurements of thrust are reported in the community elsewhere. This work represents a step toward a theory-experiment loop in which AI agents assist with experimental measurements and theoretical calculations, and synthesize insights by comparing the results, thereby accelerating the cycle that drives discovery in fundamental physics. Our work suggests that precision physics, leveraging the open LEP data and advanced theoretical landscape, provides an ideal testing ground for developing AI agent systems for scientific applications.

item.title: Prospects for Precision $YN$ and $\bar{n}N$ Measurements with an LH$_2$/LD$_2$ Target in the BESIII Detector
item.description: arXiv:2603.16075v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Tagged hyperon and antineutron beams from $J/\psi$ and $\psi(3686)$ decays allow BESIII to study (anti)hyperon--nucleon ($YN$) and antineutron--nucleon ($\bar{n}N$) scattering, but the present measurements use the beam pipe as the target, whose only free protons are in a thin cooling-oil layer. We present a conceptual feasibility study of a liquid hydrogen (LH$_2$) or liquid deuterium (LD$_2$) target between the beam pipe and the Cylindrical Gas Electron Multiplier Inner Tracker. Relative to the beam pipe, a 30~mm LH$_2$ layer increases the effective free-proton areal density by factors of 7--22 for $\Lambda$, $\Sigma^{+}$, $\Xi$, and $\bar n$ beams (3.4 for $\Omega^-$). A 30~mm LD$_2$ layer gives 0.9--2.9 times the effective neutron areal density for the same beams (0.4 for $\Omega^-$) and replaces the composite Be, C, and Au nuclei with the deuteron. These ratios characterize the target itself and do not include channel-dependent efficiencies, backgrounds, or deuteron corrections. In detector simulations without localized support material, the target affects tracking mainly below 0.5~GeV/$c$; above this momentum, proton, kaon, and pion efficiencies stay within 1.6 percentage points of the baseline. In a signal-only full-event simulation of $\bar np\to2\pi^+\pi^-$, the LH$_2$-to-beam-pipe selection-efficiency ratio is 0.86, and the vertex and energy-closure resolutions are comparable to those for beam-pipe interactions. An internal LH$_2$/LD$_2$ target is thus a promising concept for higher-statistics and less model-dependent $YN$ and $\bar nN$ measurements at BESIII, requiring further engineering and channel-level validation.
item.dc:creator: Zhao-Ling Zhang, Xu Gao, Wei-Min Song, Chang-Zheng Yuan

item.title: Machine Can Automatically Discover Parametric Functions to Model HEP Data
item.description: arXiv:2607.19750v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In HEP data analyses, finding an adequate function to model binned data has largely relied on a manual process: guess a functional form by intuition, fit, examine, then repeat until successful. We show that this iterative process can be automated by a machine using symbolic regression, which performs a data-driven search over function space without requiring prior knowledge of what an adequate function should look like. We present the SymbolFit package, which pairs symbolic regression with uncertainty modeling to target HEP analysis use cases, and demonstrate it on the CMS and ATLAS Run 2 dijet spectra: 560 independent seeded runs across seven simple fit configurations generated over 1000 functions fitting the spectra with $\chi^2/\text{NDF}\approx 1$, and 111 of the runs rediscovered the very dijet and UA2 functions used in published dijet searches.
item.dc:creator: Ho Fung Tsoi, Dylan Rankin, Cecile Caillol, Miles Cranmer, Sridhara Dasu, Javier Duarte, Philip Harris, Elliot Lipeles

item.title: Exploring ESS$\nu$SB Near Water Cherenkov Detector Designs Through Graph Neural Network Flavour Identification
item.description: arXiv:2608.23773v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The ESS$\nu$SB experiment aims to measure CP violation in the leptonic sector with high precision, necessitating robust reconstruction of neutrino events in the water Cherenkov (WC) detectors. In this work, we investigate the flavour identification potential of the proposed near WC detector using graph neural network (GNN)-based classification, with a focus on variations of key detector design parameters. In particular, we study whether a smaller and/or less instrumented detector can achieve the required classification performance. Using detailed Monte Carlo simulations of charged-current (CC) neutrino interactions, we train GNN classifiers to distinguish electron and muon neutrino CC events. We find that GNN-based classification remains accurate even for detector configurations with volumes up to a factor of eight smaller than the nominal design, with only moderate degradation in classification efficiency at fixed background rejection. The resulting loss in efficiency can largely be compensated by increased exposure time. Furthermore, we demonstrate that reduced photomultiplier tube (PMT) coverage in the nominal detector has a limited impact on classification performance, provided that coverage is maintained in regions of highest signal yield, in particular near the forward end-cap.

item.title: Gravitational waves from cosmic superstrings and gauge strings
item.description: arXiv:2312.10455v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We perform a phenomenological comparison of the gravitational wave (GW) spectrum expected from cosmic gauge string networks and superstring networks comprised of multiple string types. We show how violations of scaling behavior and the evolution of the number of relativistic degrees of freedom in the early Universe affect the GW spectrum. We derive simple analytical expressions for the GW spectrum from superstrings and gauge strings that are valid for all frequencies relevant to pulsar timing arrays (PTAs) and laser interferometers. We analyze the latest data from PTAs and show that superstring networks are consistent with 32 nHz data from NANOGrav, but are excluded by 3.2 nHz data at $3\sigma$ unless the string coupling $g_s<0.2$ or the strings evolve in only about 10% of the volume of the higher-dimensional space. We also point out that while gauge string networks are excluded by NANOGrav-15 data at $3\sigma$, they are completely compatible with EPTA and PPTA data. Finally, we study correlations between GW signals at PTAs and laser interferometers.

item.title: SparsePixels: Efficient Convolution for Sparse Data on FPGAs
item.description: arXiv:2512.06208v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Inference of standard convolutional neural networks (CNNs) on FPGAs often incurs high latency and a long initiation interval due to the deep nested loops required to densely convolve every input pixel regardless of its feature value. However, input features can be spatially sparse in some image data, where semantic information may occupy only a small fraction of the pixels and most computation would be wasted on empty regions. In this work, we introduce SparsePixels, a framework that implements sparse convolution on FPGAs by selectively retaining and computing on a small subset of active input pixels while ignoring the rest, reducing the per-layer compute from $O(HWK^2C_{\text{in}}C_{\text{out}})$ to $O(n^2C_{\text{in}}C_{\text{out}})$ and the storage from $O(HWC)$ to $O(nC)$ when $n^2\ll HW$. Because computation always runs over a single pre-specified pixel budget that is frozen at synthesis, the inference latency is data-independent and constant at runtime. We show that, for identifying neutrino interactions in naturally sparse LArTPC images with 4k pixels, a standard CNN with a compact size of 4k parameters incurs an inference latency of 48.665 $\mu$s on an FPGA, whereas a sparse CNN of the same base architecture, computing on less than 1% of the input pixels, achieves a $\times 73$ speedup to 0.665 $\mu$s with resource utilization well within on-chip budgets, trading only a small percent-level performance loss. This work aims to benefit future algorithm development for efficient data readout in modern experiments with strict latency requirements of microseconds or below.
item.dc:creator: Ho Fung Tsoi, Dylan Rankin, Vladimir Loncar, Philip Harris

item.title: Resurgence in scalar and spinor QED: The Euler-Heisenberg Lagrangian in parallel field backgrounds
item.description: arXiv:2512.22775v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present the first systematic resurgent analysis of the Euler--Heisenberg Lagrangian in spinor and scalar quantum electrodynamics for the most general constant background field configuration. In contrast to the extensively studied case of the perpendicular electric and magnetic fields configuration, the parallel fields configuration exhibits unique asymptotic structures, leading to a substantially richer pattern of singularities in the Borel plane. Explicit large-order asymptotic formulas for the weak-field coefficients in both spinor and scalar quantum electrodynamics are derived. These reveal a nontrivial interplay between alternating and non-alternating factorial growth, governed by distinct structures associated with electric and magnetic contributions, and smoothly interpolating between the known perpendicular fields limit. Using Borel--dispersion techniques, we demonstrate that the complete instanton structure underlying Schwinger pair production in parallel fields backgrounds is encoded in the divergent perturbative coefficients. We then construct resurgent approximants using Pad\'{e}--Borel and Pad\'{e}--Conformal--Borel resummation schemes adapted to the parallel fields configuration. For the spinor case, conformal improvement results in a significant enhancement in reconstructing both the real and imaginary parts of the effective Lagrangian across a wide range of field ratios. Detailed comparisons with exact special-function representations demonstrate the reliability of reconstructions from a modest number of weak-field coefficients. This work establishes a natural completion of the resurgence programme for constant electromagnetic backgrounds, providing a robust analytic framework for exploring non-perturbative physics and strong-field phenomena in spinor and scalar quantum electrodynamics, from finite perturbative data.
item.dc:creator: Drishti Gupta, Arun Thalapillil

item.title: Optomechanical Detection of Individual Gas Collisions
item.description: arXiv:2604.18371v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We experimentally demonstrate the detection of momentum transfers from individual collisions of Kr, Xe, and SF$_6$ with an optically levitated nanoparticle, finding good agreement with theoretical expectations. The observed event rates accurately measure the gas partial pressures, while the spectral shape provides a sensitive probe of the surface properties of the nanoparticle, including its temperature. The reconstruction of impulse signals as small as 200 keV/$c$ further establishes that levitated optomechanical sensors can reach the sensitivity required for precision measurements of fundamental particle interactions, and demonstrates a proof-of-principle for a primary pressure sensor based on the detection of individual gas particle collisions.
item.dc:creator: Yu-Han Tseng, Clarke A. Hardy, T. W. Penny, Cecily Lowe, Jacqueline Baeza-Rubio, Daniel Carney, David C. Moore

item.title: Optical effects in Gaseous Electron Multipliers (GEMs)
item.description: arXiv:2604.27399v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Optical time projection chambers (OTPCs) are well suited for applications that require the highest spatial resolution for particle track reconstruction. The MIGDAL experiment uses a glass GEM-based OTPC and observes a systematic excess in both the intensity and width of particle tracks in its optical readout, when compared with charge readout simulations. One hypothesis is that scintillation light produced inside a GEM hole during the avalanche propagates through the GEM substrate and exits neighboring holes. We present lab measurements testing this hypothesized optical broadening effect in three types of GEM substrates: glass, ceramic, and FR4. Our observations quantify this optical broadening and demonstrate it to be strongest in glass GEMs. Additionally, we use Geant4 simulations to both reproduce our observations and quantify optical broadening effects in realistic charge avalanches. Applying our glass GEM effects to simulated particle tracks yields increases of track intensity and widths by up to approximately 26% and 31%, respectively. This may explain the larger-than-expected track intensities and widths observed in the MIGDAL OTPC. This effect may be relevant to GEM-based OTPCs, with its magnitude depending on the GEM structure and detector-specific optical configuration.
item.dc:creator: D. Edgeman, F. M. Brunbauer, M. Gardner, D. Loomba, P. A. Majewski, T. Marley, L. Millins, T. Neep, K. Nikolopoulos, J. Schueler, E. Tilly, W. Thompson

item.title: Dark Matter Particle Explorer: Ten-Year On-Orbit Performance and Scientific Outcomes
item.description: arXiv:2610.21168v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The Dark Matter Particle Explorer (DAMPE, also known as ``Wukong'') is the first scientific space mission within the framework of the Strategic Pioneer Program on Space Science of the Chinese Academy of Sciences. The main scientific objectives of DAMPE include indirect detection of dark matter, cosmic-ray physics, and high energy gamma-ray astronomy. Thanks to its large geometrical factor and thick imaging calorimeter, DAMPE could effectively detect cosmic-ray electrons (including positrons) and gamma-rays up to 10~TeV, and nuclei up to PeV. Since launched on 17 December 2015 into a Sun-synchronous orbit, DAMPE has been smoothly operating on orbit for more than ten years. Here we present an overview of instrument, on-orbit status, and highlight scientific results of DAMPE, including the measurements of the all-electron energy spectrum and the spectra of protons and other nuclei, and high energy gamma-ray line search.
item.dc:creator: Jian-Hua Guo, Chuan Yue, Yun-Long Zhang, Yi-Zhong Fan, Jin Chang
